title: Acute chest pain
priority: Second most common ED reason for visit in NHAMCS fact sheets.
gate_note: One normal ECG or one early troponin does not rule out ACS; patient characteristics must not be used to dismiss the complaint.

title: Acute shortness of breath
priority: Among the top ED reasons for visit in NHAMCS fact sheets.
gate_note: Gate wording is a structural convention, not taken from a source.

title: Acute lower abdominal or pelvic pain
population: Adults, including women of reproductive age
priority: Abdominal pain is the leading ED reason for visit in NHAMCS fact sheets.
gate_note: Urgent causes to consider first in women of reproductive age include ectopic pregnancy, ruptured ovarian cyst, ovarian torsion, appendicitis and pelvic inflammatory disease.

title: Acute nontraumatic headache
priority: Among the top five ED reasons for visit in NHAMCS fact sheets.
gate_note: Most headaches are primary, but secondary causes must be screened for first.

title: Fever in an adult (suspected sepsis)
priority: Fever is among the top ED reasons for visit in NHAMCS fact sheets.
gate_note: Updated to the 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign guideline, which replaced the 2021 edition.

title: Syncope (transient loss of consciousness)
priority: Common ED presentation with its own US and European guidelines.
gate_note: Not all high-risk patients need admission; risk scores may be reasonable but are not better than clinical judgment.

title: Upper gastrointestinal bleeding
priority: GI bleeding causes more than half a million US admissions a year.
gate_note: This situation is mostly risk triage; the cause is found at endoscopy rather than eliminated step by step.

title: Unilateral leg swelling or pain (suspected DVT)
priority: High-volume VTE presentation with a GRADE guideline.
gate_note: Diagnostic strategy depends on the estimated pre-test probability.

title: Acute dizziness or vertigo
priority: Common ED complaint with a 2023 GRADE guideline.
gate_note: Untrained clinicians apply and interpret HINTS inaccurately; GRACE-3 recommends training.

title: Acute focal neurologic deficit (suspected stroke)
population: Adults (the 2026 guideline also adds pediatric guidance, not encoded here)
gate_note: Verified against the 2026 AHA/ASA guideline, which replaced the 2018 guideline and 2019 update.

title: Acute low back pain
priority: Leading cause of disability under age 45; imaging overuse is a known problem.
gate_note: Most uncomplicated acute low back pain needs no imaging.

title: Acute flank pain (suspected stone)
priority: Has a dedicated ACR topic with four variants.
